- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for momentum bias.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.
- In high-event periods (≥18 events/30d), model overestimates short-term volatility; cap forecast range within ±2% of recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.00 to -1.00), model fails to adjust quickly; apply 1–2 day lag correction to avoid false peaks.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, apply mean reversion: pull forecast toward prior 14-day average by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- In high-bearish sentiment + high supply net, model often ignores policy context; reduce forecast by 1–3% for each bearish sentiment >0.50 and supply net < -10.00.
